title: Add init throttler and namespace quota prober with strict values schema and example transforms
author: Maya Brooks
description:
Motivation:
Private installs have caused control-plane/api-server bursts during large multi-tenant upgrades and initial tenant bootstrap. Customers on constrained clusters (on-prem and small VPCs) observed API throttling and failed migrations when many init jobs ran concurrently. This PR adds two coordinated defenses: (1) an init-throttler helm hook that sequences init jobs using a lightweight leader-election+token-bucket pattern, and (2) a namespace quota-prober init container and probe which validates namespace resource quotas before starting migrations or heavy init work.

What this PR does (high-level):
- Introduces chart/templates/init-throttler.yaml: a new optional Helm hook that, when enabled, deploys a small init controller Job which provides a ConfigMap-based token queue used by tenant init Jobs to acquire a slot before proceeding. Slots and backoff are configurable from values.
- Adds chart/values.schema.json with JSON Schema validation for new keys and stricter typing of existing fields (affinityProfiles, init, preflight). The schema includes enums and constraints to prevent common misconfigurations (e.g., setting both nodeSelector and affinityProfiles contradictory configs).
- Adds chart/values.yaml examples showing how to opt into throttling, tune slots/per-second, and enable the quotaProbe for low-resource clusters.
- Adds chart/templates/quota-prober-init.yaml: init container template that runs a small probe to check namespace resourceQuota and node allocatable before allowing init to continue. The probe integrates with the throttler token flow but can run independently.
- Adds scripts/helm-utils.sh helper for building a values transform used in upgrades: it can safely migrate older boolean-style flags into the stricter schema (example transform included).
- Updates docs/upgrade-notes.md with guidance for toggling the throttler and guidance for troubleshooting probe failures.

Design notes and rationale:
- We intentionally use a ConfigMap+leader-election approach rather than a custom controller to keep the runtime footprint minimal and acceptable for air-gapped/on-prem installs. The token-bucket semantics are optimistic (best-effort): if the ConfigMap update fails transiently the job will retry with exponential backoff.
- The quota-prober is a small read-only probe that checks for the presence of a ResourceQuota and compares hard limits against a configurable threshold. This avoids starting large init tasks when cluster quotas would immediately block them.
- The values.schema.json both protects users from invalid shapes and enables Helm 3 validation in CI for private installs. The schema also documents deprecated fields and provides transformation guidance.

Backward compatibility and upgrade path:
- Default behavior is off: both throttler and quota-prober are disabled by default. Existing installs are not changed unless operators opt in or upgrade with the transform script.
- scripts/helm-utils.sh contains a safe migrate_values() routine that will run as a preflight step in our private-installer pipeline; it converts old flags (e.g., init.enableLegacyHook: true) into the new names and warns on collisions. Operators should run the transform in a staging environment before production.

Testing and verification:
- Unit tests for the values schema added under chart/tests/schema-validation (helm plugin).
- End-to-end helm test harness added: helm test --cleanup exercises a 3-tenant local scenario with throttler enabled (jobs sequentialized) and quota-prober toggled to fail to validate failure modes.
- CI: initial CI run failed lint due to an overly permissive schema reference; fix made in second commit. Final CI matrix: lint, unit-schema, helm-integration (k3s job) all passed.

Operational considerations:
- Observability: throttler emits token-acquire metrics to a ConfigMap-backed index and logs at INFO when a tenant waits > 30s. We added two metrics for SLOs: "init_throttle_wait_seconds" and "quota_prober_failures_total". These are scraped via the existing metrics-exporter sidecar in private installs when enabled.
- Failure modes: if the kube-apiserver is unavailable, throttler retries with exponential backoff; stuck tokens are garbage-collected after the configured tokenTTL. Quota probe failures surface as pod conditions, and the installer can be configured to either pause and require manual reconciliation or continue with a conservative fallback.

Files changed (summary):
- chart/templates/init-throttler.yaml (new)
- chart/templates/quota-prober-init.yaml (new)
- chart/values.schema.json (new/updated)
- chart/values.yaml (examples updated)
- scripts/helm-utils.sh (new helper + migrate_values)
- docs/upgrade-notes.md (appendix)
- chart/tests/helm-integration.yaml (test harness)

Related work: linked Linear tasks ENG-2219 (throttled init design), ENG-2381 (quota prober follow-up). Related support ticket SUP-1142 reported a production incident where 23 tenant init jobs caused API throttling in a constrained cluster.

How to roll out (operator guidance):
1) In staging, enable throttler with conservative slots: values:private.initThrottler.enabled=true, slots=2, slotsPerSecond=0.5.
2) Run scripts/helm-utils.sh migrate_values --in values-old.yaml --out values-new.yaml and inspect warnings.
3) Deploy, monitor the init_throttle_wait_seconds metric and quota_prober_failures_total. If many waits are observed, gradually increase slots.
4) Once validated, roll to production with a canary namespace first.

Backout plan: disable private.initThrottler.enabled and/or enable private.initThrottler.drainOnDisable to allow running tokens to finish then stop new acquisitions. Quota probe can be set to warn-only by setting checkMode = "warn" in values to avoid blocking.

Note on security and RBAC: all new resources use namespace-scoped RBAC roles and do not grant cluster-wide privileges. The ConfigMap used by throttler lives in the target namespace.

Add quota-prober init container and probe logic
Add values.schema.json and migration helper script; update docs and tests
review_comments: Evan Li: Can we avoid ConfigMap churn under heavy scale? Suggest using annotation-batched updates and a tokenTTL; responded and implemented tokenTTL + batch window.
Sana Iyer: Schema looks good but please add explicit enum for affinityProfiles to avoid accidental misconfigs; added in second commit.
Jonah Park: CI failed on lint on first run due to $ref path; fixed in commit 3 and reran CI. Approving after helm-integration passes.
release_notes: New optional init throttler for sequenced tenant init jobs; optional namespace quota-prober to prevent starting heavy init work when quotas would block it; JSON Schema for stricter values validation; migration helper script to transform older values files.
